title: Benchmarking deep learning variant callers on long-read data
abstract: We compare a deep learning variant caller with two statistical callers on 30x Oxford Nanopore whole-genome sequencing from 12 human reference samples with curated truth sets. The deep learning caller reaches an F1 of 0.997 for SNVs and 0.91 for indels, outperforming both statistical callers on indels in homopolymer regions. Runtime on a single GPU is 3.1 hours per genome.

title: A single-cell atlas of soybean root nodules
abstract: We profile 41,000 nuclei from soybean root nodules at four time points after rhizobia inoculation using single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Clustering identifies 17 cell populations, including two infected-cell states with distinct nitrogen-fixation expression programs. The atlas is released with an interactive browser for the legume research community.

title: Rapid exome sequencing in a neonatal intensive care unit
abstract: We report a two-year prospective study of rapid exome sequencing for 214 critically ill infants with suspected genetic disorders. A diagnostic variant was identified in 38% of cases with a median turnaround of 5 days, and results changed clinical management for 61% of diagnosed infants. We describe the variant interpretation workflow and its costs.

title: Population structure of a declining prairie grouse
abstract: Using low-coverage whole-genome sequencing of 380 birds from 22 sites across the Midwest, we estimate population structure and effective population size for a declining prairie grouse. Genetic diversity is lowest in the most isolated fragments, and demographic modeling suggests declines began about 150 years ago, consistent with grassland conversion.

title: DNA methylation clocks in dairy cattle
abstract: We generate reduced-representation bisulfite sequencing profiles for 1,150 dairy cows aged 1 to 12 years and train an elastic-net epigenetic clock. Predicted age correlates with chronological age at r = 0.94 on held-out animals, and animals with accelerated epigenetic age have shorter productive lifespans.

title: Metagenomic surveillance of antibiotic resistance genes in wastewater
abstract: We sequence 520 wastewater samples collected weekly from 10 treatment plants over one year using shotgun metagenomics. We detect 1,340 distinct antibiotic resistance genes, with resistance gene abundance peaking in late winter. Assembly-based analysis links 22% of resistance genes to plasmids, suggesting potential for horizontal transfer.

title: Genome-wide CRISPR screen for drought tolerance genes in maize protoplasts
abstract: We perform a pooled CRISPR knockout screen targeting 9,800 maize genes in leaf protoplasts under osmotic stress. Guide RNA depletion analysis identifies 64 candidate genes, 11 of which we validate in stable transgenic lines grown under field drought conditions. Candidates are enriched for stomatal regulation and abscisic acid signaling.

title: Chromatin accessibility across human immune cell types
abstract: Using ATAC-seq on 26 sorted immune cell types from 40 healthy donors, we map 310,000 accessible chromatin regions. Cell-type-specific regions are enriched near genes with matching expression, and 18% of regions show accessibility differences associated with donor age. All data are deposited in a public repository.

title: Gut microbiome changes during a high-fiber dietary intervention
abstract: In a 10-week randomized trial with 96 adults, we compare a high-fiber diet with a control diet and profile stool samples every two weeks using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing. The high-fiber group shows a 2.4-fold increase in short-chain-fatty-acid producing taxa, and these shifts are reversed within four weeks after the intervention ends.

title: Spatial transcriptomics of the developing mouse cortex
abstract: We apply a spatial transcriptomics platform to 48 brain sections from embryonic and early postnatal mice, measuring expression of 18,000 genes at near single-cell resolution. We map the spatial order in which neuronal subtypes appear and identify a transient progenitor zone that disappears by postnatal day 7.

title: Assembling a telomere-to-telomere genome for a wild tomato relative
abstract: Combining PacBio HiFi reads, ultra-long nanopore reads, and Hi-C scaffolding, we assemble a gap-free 1.1-gigabase genome for a drought-tolerant wild tomato relative. Comparison with cultivated tomato reveals 312 structural variants overlapping annotated genes, including expansions in a family of disease-resistance genes.

title: Language models for predicting the effect of missense variants
abstract: We fine-tune a protein language model on 2.3 million missense variants with experimental fitness measurements from deep mutational scanning studies. On held-out proteins the model's predictions correlate with measured fitness at a median Spearman rho of 0.52, outperforming conservation-based scores, and run in seconds per protein on a single GPU.

title: Ancient DNA reveals livestock movements in prehistoric Europe
abstract: We sequence ancient DNA from 141 cattle and sheep bones dating from 6000 to 2000 BCE across 30 archaeological sites. Mitochondrial and low-coverage nuclear genomes show at least two waves of livestock introduction into northern Europe, separated by roughly 1,500 years.

title: Long-read RNA sequencing of alternative splicing in the human heart
abstract: Using PacBio long-read RNA sequencing of 34 left-ventricle samples, we catalog 52,000 full-length transcript isoforms, 29% of which are absent from reference annotations. Novel isoforms are enriched in sarcomere genes, and isoform usage differs between failing and non-failing hearts for 410 genes.

title: Soil metagenomes under long-term nitrogen fertilization
abstract: We sequence soil metagenomes from a 40-year field experiment comparing five nitrogen fertilization rates. Higher nitrogen rates reduce the abundance of nitrogen-fixation genes by up to 45% and shift community composition toward fast-growing taxa. We recover 230 metagenome-assembled genomes, 60 of which represent previously undescribed species.

title: Scalable variant calling for biobank-scale cohorts on GPUs
abstract: We port a germline variant calling pipeline to GPUs and process 25,000 whole genomes from a biobank cohort. End-to-end processing takes 22 minutes per genome on one node with four GPUs versus 9 hours on CPUs, with concordance above 99.9% to the CPU results. Joint genotyping across the cohort completes in under two days.
